prerequisite_rule: You need the Wingspan base game; this box adds cards and parts only.
what_it_adds: 81 new European birds, many with powers that trigger at round end. Also 5 bonus cards, 5 goal tiles, purple eggs and a card tray.
what_it_fixes: Gives more ways to score in the last round, so piling up eggs is not the only big finish.
verdict_reason: More birds with no new rules. IGN and Fjord Labs both say get Oceania first, then add this for variety.
notes: Price is Stonemaier webstore price shown on product page. Retail release Nov 22 2019 (SKU STM901).

prerequisite_rule: You need the Wingspan base game; no other expansion is needed.
what_it_adds: 95 new birds, new player mats, a wild food called nectar, new dice, 5 bonus cards, 4 goal tiles and yellow eggs.
what_it_fixes: New mats let you pay to refresh the bird tray or feeder, and nectar makes it easier to afford birds.
verdict_reason: The one most reviewers say to get first. The new mats and nectar change the game more than any other box.
notes: MSRP $35 per Jamey Stegmaier comment (Jun 22 2026) on product page; webstore shows $32. 17 nectar birds need the new mats/dice. ASIN from amazon.com/dp link titled Stonemaier-Games-Wingspan-Oceania-Expansion on BGQ review.

prerequisite_rule: Plays alone as a 1-2 player game; the 6-7 player Flock mode needs player pieces from the base game.
what_it_adds: 90 new birds, 14 bonus cards, a 2-player Duet map, and Flock mode for 6-7 players. Works as its own 1-2 player game.
what_it_fixes: Adds head-to-head interaction to 2-player games and a way to seat 6-7 players.
verdict_reason: Best if you mostly play with two, since it works on its own. Reviewers call the 6-7 player Flock mode messy.
notes: Price is Stonemaier webstore price. SKU STM906. Duet end-round goals only for 2p mode. ASIN from amazon.com/dp link titled 'Stonemaier Games: Wingspan Asia' on Meeple Mountain review.

prerequisite_rule: You need either the Wingspan base game or Wingspan Asia (for 1-2 players).
what_it_adds: 111 new Latin American birds, 40 small hummingbird cards, a hummingbird garden board, mat overlays and tracks, 8 bonus cards.
what_it_fixes: Hummingbirds give a small bonus at the end of each row, so every turn does a bit more.
verdict_reason: Newest box. Board Game Quest calls it a must-buy with rules that slot in easily. Games run a little longer.
notes: US price not shown (page lists AUD $45 only). US online retail release Mar 13 2026. Hummingbird module does not scale to Flock 6-7p; Flock add-on announced for Oct 2026. Only one verdict source read.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Terraforming Mars base game; it mixes with any other expansion.
what_it_adds: Prelude cards that give each player a head start, plus 5 new corporations and 7 project cards.
verdict_reason: Both rankings we read put it first. It cuts the slow opening rounds and adds almost no rules.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Terraforming Mars base game; other expansions are optional.
what_it_adds: Colony tiles for moons you can settle and trade with, plus new cards and corporations.
what_it_fixes: Gives you something useful to do when the card market is dry.
verdict_reason: The usual second buy. It adds some rules, so get used to the base game first.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Terraforming Mars base game.
what_it_adds: A double-sided board with two new Mars maps, each with its own milestones and awards.
what_it_fixes: Freshens up the board once the base map feels familiar.
verdict_reason: New maps, no new rules. Buy it once the base map feels worn out.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Terraforming Mars base game.
what_it_adds: Venus as a fourth track to raise, about 50 project cards, 5 corporations, and a new floater resource.
verdict_reason: Adds cards and a fourth track but makes games longer. Skip it if your games already run long.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Terraforming Mars base game.
what_it_adds: A political committee with parties and delegates, global event cards, and new corporations and projects.
verdict_reason: For groups with many games behind them who want politics. Both rankings put it last because it adds the most rules and time.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Everdell base game.
what_it_adds: A river board, frog ambassadors, pearls to collect, Wonders to build, and new water critters and cards.
what_it_fixes: Gives you a big goal to build toward beyond your 15-card city.
verdict_reason: King Panda ranks it first, but Meeple Mountain found the race for Wonders pulls focus from the base game. Great if you want a new goal; less so if you like the base game as is.
notes: Tycoon store listing is 2nd edition. Player count with expansion not stated on publisher page. 1-4 players per Amazon listing title. Reviewers split on buy order.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Everdell base game.
what_it_adds: A train station, ticket tiles, visitor cards, a second board, and 100+ new cards with new critters.
what_it_fixes: Adds more face-up cards to pick from as the deck grows.
verdict_reason: The safest pick: more of the same game, done well. Meeple Mountain ranks it the best boxed expansion and King Panda ranks it second.

prerequisite_rule: You need the Everdell base game; it works with all other expansions.
what_it_adds: Nightweave, a spider opponent for solo or 2-player games, plus the Corrin Evertail, Legends II and Through Every Season packs.
what_it_fixes: Gives solo and 2-player games a smarter rival than the base game's solo opponent.
verdict_reason: Top pick if you play solo or with two. Both rankings like it, but it matters less for bigger groups.
notes: 1-2 players refers to the Nightweave modes; other content mixes into normal games. Includes Corrin Evertail, Legends II, Through Every Season (not sold separately here).

prerequisite_rule: You need the Everdell base game.
what_it_adds: A mountain board, weather cards, Big Critter mounts, discovery cards, maps and expeditions.
verdict_reason: Opinions split. Weather and Big Critters suit groups that like surprises; planners may find it frustrating.
notes: Tycoon listing is 2nd edition. 1-4 players per Amazon listing title. Release year not confirmed (funded Kickstarter Sep 2019).

prerequisite_rule: You need the Everdell base game.
what_it_adds: Parts for 5-6 players, 15 player power cards, a shared Market board, Garland Awards and special event goals.
verdict_reason: Only needed if you often play with 5-6. Both rankings put it last among the big boxes.
notes: Showing sold out on Tycoon store on 2026-09-27. 1-6 players per Wikipedia. Release year not confirmed (funded Kickstarter Sep 2019).

prerequisite_rule: Includes the base game, so nothing else is needed.
what_it_adds: Everdell plus Pearlbrook, Spirecrest, Bellfaire, Newleaf, Mistwood, Collector's Edition content, storage trays and one rulebook.
verdict_reason: Only if you know you want everything. It is heavy and costly, and one reviewer skipped it because he only uses one expansion at a time.
notes: 1-6 players because it includes Bellfaire (per Wikipedia). Smithsonian listed it among best games of 2022; Meeple Mountain author passed on it.
